newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's gas firm to join Russian, German JVs.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's gas firm to join Russian, German JVs.

text.p: Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet on Thursday gave a green light to the country's gas monopolist Bulgargas to join two Bulgarian-German joint stock firms and another Bulgarian-Russian venture, state radio said.
Moscow and Sofia plan to set up a joint venture, which will settle part of Bulgaria's payments of Russian gas supplies by barter.
Bulgaria has offered Russia's Gazprom a list of goods and services to be supplied to Russia against part of the natural gas. The list includes medicines, cigarettes, spirits and fork lift trucks.
The two sides will share the stakes in the planned venture, Bulgargas officials said.

Bulgargas will have 40 percent in the venture and Bulgaria's Biochim Bank will hold a 10-percent stake. The Russian side will be represented by Stolichnii Bank Sberejenie with 10 percent stake and a further Russian firm.
Bulgaria will receive 3.34 billion cubic metres of Russian gas each year until 2008 under a 20-year intergovernmental agreement and must pay for them in cash.
For the first 10 years of the agreement, which expires this year, Russia has supplied Bulgaria with gas in return for its participation in construction work at Russia's Jambourg gas field.
Bulgargas officials did not give details on the two Bulgarian-German joint stock companies.
The government, which is Bulgargas' principal, has also released the executive director of the state-owned Bulgargas Petar Sabev at his request because of his health condition, officials said.
